item.title: Less Experience Leads to Faster Neural Adaptation
item.description: A new study finds that the brain learns better from spaced-out, rare events than from constant repetition, challenging 100 years of Pavlovian theory.

item.title: Hypothalamus Signal Build Endurance After Exercise
item.description: A new study reveals that SF1 neurons in the hypothalamus are required for the body to gain endurance after exercise, acting as a master coordinator for muscle remodeling.

item.title: Second Pregnancy Rewires Mom’s Brain for Multi-Child Parenting
item.description: One and done? Not for your neurons. Scientists have discovered that a second pregnancy leaves its own unique mark on the brain, specifically tuning it for the chaos of multi-child parenting.

item.title: The Oxytocin Switch That Controls Your Social Vibe
item.description: It’s the brain’s social thermostat. Scientists have discovered the protein that controls the slow, steady drip of oxytocin that works alongside serotonin to prime us for human connection.

item.title: Processed Foods Silence the Brain’s Fear Center
item.description: Three days is all it takes. New research proves that skipping fiber can trigger rapid inflammation in your brain's emotional center, leaving you vulnerable to poor decisions.

item.title: Blood Test Can Predict When Alzheimer’s Symptoms Will Start
item.description: A new study reveals a p-tau217 "blood clock" that predicts the onset of Alzheimer’s symptoms within three to four years.

item.title: Twin Enzymes Rewire Your Brain for Interaction and Memory
item.description: Twin enzymes, different worlds. Scientists have discovered that MNK1 and MNK2 act as the brain's specialized switches for memory and social curiosity.

item.title: Satiety Bypass: How Cannabis Overrides the Brain’s “I’m Full” Signal
item.description: A new study reveals how cannabis hijacks the brain's hypothalamus to trigger "the munchies," offering new insights for treating medical appetite loss.

item.title: Ghost in the Machine: Exposing the Hidden Personalities of AI
item.description: Researchers develop a method to expose and steer hidden concepts, biases, and personalities within Large Language Models (LLMs).

item.title: Peripheral Eye Scan Catch Alzheimer’s in Its Tracks
item.description: Researchers find that early Alzheimer’s markers appear in the peripheral retina, offering a new path for non-invasive early detection.
